picks.title: OpenAI’s chief scientist has thoughts on how to limit AI development
picks.post: Before anyone sets a speed limit on AI development, someone has to agree on how to measure speed. Good luck with that one.
picks.reason: OpenAI's chief scientist on AI pacing, a sharp framing of the regulation debate.
picks.card_text: Speed limit needs an agreed measure of speed

picks.title: Europe's STOXX 600 rises as tech shares rebound after AI-driven rout
picks.post: Tech shares bounced back after an AI-driven rout, which is the market's way of saying it has already forgotten last week. Give it a few days.
picks.reason: Market-level signal on AI stock sentiment after a sharp selloff.
picks.card_text: Tech shares rebound after AI-driven rout

picks.title: How Notable Capital, GIC, and Baillie Gifford bet big on Anthropic before its IPO
picks.post: Notable Capital, GIC and Baillie Gifford explain why they bet billions on Anthropic before its IPO. Conviction is cheap to describe in hindsight; the IPO price will do the grading.
picks.reason: Pre-IPO backers of Anthropic detailing big bets, relevant to frontier AI valuations.
picks.card_text: Backers bet billions before Anthropic's IPO

picks.title: Insight: How Nvidia’s billion-dollar turnaround in China is threatened by Huang’s exit
picks.post: Nvidia's billion-dollar China turnaround is now threatened by Jensen Huang's exit. So the comeback depended on one person's calendar. Curious how much of it survives without him.
picks.reason: Nvidia China revenue recovery at risk from leadership change; directly relevant to the chip market.
picks.card_text: Billion-dollar China turnaround, now at risk

picks.title: The Enigma of SoftBank’s $1 Trillion SK Hynix Buyout Attempt
picks.post: SoftBank floated a $1 trillion buyout of SK Hynix, which EE Times says was a non-starter from the start. Still, it shows how badly everyone wants memory capacity for the AI buildout.
picks.reason: Shows strategic value of memory chipmakers in the AI buildout, even for a deal that never had a chance.

picks.title: Consortium in talks to buy LCY's $600 million China chip chemicals business, people say
picks.post: A consortium is reportedly in talks for LCY's $600 million China chip chemicals business. Everyone wants a piece of the chip supply chain, just not the parts that make the headlines.
picks.reason: Chip materials M&A in China; a supply-chain signal, though a smaller story.

picks.title: Over half of all console players active on GTA 6's launch day played it, says Circana
picks.post: Circana says more than half of everyone playing on PS5 and Xbox on GTA 6's launch day was playing GTA 6. Impressive reach, though nobody has measured how many of those players were just ignoring the rest of their library.
picks.reason: Concrete platform-wide engagement figure from a credible market tracker.
picks.card_text: More than half of console players, launch day

picks.title: Unreal Engine 6 to jettison key scripting feature earlier than planned in favor of AI coding
picks.post: Unreal Engine 6 will drop Blueprints earlier than planned in favor of AI coding. Visual scripting existed so people didn't have to write code, so retiring it for a tool that writes code is an interesting choice.
picks.reason: Major engine platform shift toward AI-assisted development, affecting many studios.
picks.card_text: Blueprints cut early for AI coding

picks.title: Activision patents AI voice system that learns from in-game chat and creates audio for NPCs who can even speak in place of you
picks.post: Activision has patented a system that listens to player voice chat after key moments and recreates it for NPCs, who can speak in place of you. Turning players' trash talk into training data is a bold move from a company that still needs everyone to log in.
picks.reason: Notable AI-in-games patent tying voice chat to NPC generation; signals publisher direction.
picks.card_text: Patent: NPCs trained on player voice chat

picks.title: VC funding rebounds as startups raise $255M; Women founders driving social change
picks.post: 22 new-age tech companies made their public market debut in FY26. That's a lot of listings to justify in one year, and I'm curious how many are still trading above their issue price.
picks.reason: Concrete count of new-age tech IPOs in FY26, a clear signal for the Indian listings market.
picks.card_text: 22 new-age tech companies listed in FY26

picks.title: Sarvam clarifies AI strategy amid debate over hosting Chinese models
picks.post: Sarvam says a model's country of origin and where it runs are "two different matters." For a company pitching homegrown AI, the hosting bill is the part people will read closely.
picks.reason: Sarvam's defence of hosting Chinese models touches on sovereignty and the credibility of India's AI push.
picks.card_text: Origin and hosting are "two different matters"

picks.title: India may emerge as long-term AI winner despite dependence on foreign tech: Deutsche Bank
picks.post: Deutsche Bank says India could be one of the biggest long-term AI winners, citing population, digital infrastructure and talent. Long-term winner is a comfortable phrase for a report; the open question is who captures the value.
picks.reason: Broker view on India's AI economic upside, useful context on whether the thesis holds.
picks.card_text: One of the biggest long-term AI beneficiaries

picks.title: Capita shares plunge 70% as boss quits after civil service pensions failure
picks.post: Capita shares are down 70% after the boss quit over delayed civil service pension payments. Outsourcing a pension scheme was supposed to move the risk off the government, but the people still waiting for their money seem to be carrying it.
picks.reason: A 70% share collapse tied to a specific operational failure. Shows outsourcing risk landing on the public.

picks.title: Catering giant to switch main share listing to US in further blow to UK
picks.post: Another UK company is moving its main listing to the US, with a catering giant the latest to decide London isn't worth the trouble. Which household name gets to turn off the lights next?
picks.reason: Part of a sustained UK listing exodus, a real structural shift in capital markets.
picks.card_text: Main share listing moving to US

picks.title: Poundland is facing collapse - what's gone wrong?
picks.post: Poundland has days to find a buyer or collapse into administration. A chain built on cheap prices running out of buyers is a strange sign for a cost-of-living story.
picks.reason: Concrete distress signal for UK retail and consumer spending, with a days-long deadline.
picks.card_text: Days left to find a buyer

picks.title: GTA 6 Has Already Sold 45 Million Copies, Says Research Firm
picks.post:
A research firm claims GTA 6 has sold nearly 45 million copies in its launch weekend, worth over $4 billion.

The number comes from the research firm, not the publisher.
picks.reason: Huge number everyone can compare to their own spending; the source question invites debate.

picks.title: Metacritic's user review problem worsens, as GTA 6's launch prompts review-bombing for completely unrelated games like Soul Calibur and The Ocarina of Time
picks.post:
GTA 6's Metacritic user scores are being review-bombed, and classic games like Soul Calibur and The Ocarina of Time are getting hit too.

Eurogamer says the fight is now reaching games with no link to GTA 6 at all.
picks.reason: Fan war over user scores hitting beloved unrelated classics; people will pick sides fast.

picks.title: Binding of Isaac DLC adds AI music in GTA 6-parodying update despite not having an AI disclosure, Steam reviews drop to Overwhelmingly Negative, music gets pulled
picks.post:
Nicalis has pulled undisclosed AI-generated music from The Binding of Isaac: Repentance+ after a GTA 6 parody update went out.

Steam reviews have dropped to Overwhelmingly Negative.
picks.reason: AI music without disclosure, a backlash that tanked Steam reviews, and a publisher reversing course.

picks.title: Nvidia reverses course and brings Jensen Huang back as CEO
picks.post:
Nvidia has reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, effective immediately, after its board voted unanimously to bring him back.

The share price jumped more than 30%, and senior US government officials reportedly backed the reversal.
picks.reason: Huge name, dramatic U-turn, a 30% stock jump, and a government angle people will argue about.

picks.title: Virginia, Oregon sue Musk's SpaceX over Grok AI's creation of child sexual abuse images and videos
picks.post:
Virginia and Oregon are suing Elon Musk's SpaceX over child sexual abuse images and videos created by its Grok AI.

The states' attorneys general argue sexual images from the chatbot harmed consumers.
picks.reason: Musk, AI-generated child abuse content, and a state lawsuit; people will split on blame and on Grok.

picks.title: Uber now lets you book rides that record the drive by default
picks.post:
Uber is testing rides that record the entire trip by default, using the driver's front phone camera.

The option shows up as "Recorded Rides" in the app, and is being piloted in the US.
picks.reason: Default in-car recording raises privacy questions for both riders and drivers, a feeling everyone has.

picks.title: Pip assessments need 'fundamental overhaul', report to say
picks.post:
Poundland has days to find a buyer or collapse into administration.

A chain built on cheap prices is running out of time, and shoppers and staff are left wondering what happens next.
picks.reason: Household UK name facing a sudden collapse, with jobs and everyday prices at stake.
picks.card_text: Days to find a buyer or collapse

picks.title: Dutch privacy authority urges consumers not to buy ‘pervert glasses’
picks.post:
The Netherlands' data protection agency is urging consumers not to buy smart glasses, which it calls "pervert glasses" in its warning.

It says the wearables violate people's privacy, get information wrong and can lead to unsafe situations.
picks.reason: Privacy fears about camera glasses hit everyday people, and the 'pervert glasses' label invites debate.

picks.title: Microsoft explains the Outlook outage that hit millions
picks.post:
Microsoft says a months-old bug and a chain of cascading failures brought Outlook and other services down worldwide.

The outage hit millions, and Microsoft warns scammers are already using it to convince people their emails are lost.
picks.reason: Huge outage affecting millions plus a scam angle people will share and argue about.

picks.title: Drone attack on Colombian police base injures civilians and damages homes
picks.post:
Meta has dropped its 2030 net zero goal in its 2026 sustainability report.

The decision could send ripples across the tech industry, and it lands as climate pledges become a point of debate.
picks.reason: A big-name company abandoning a climate promise is a clear trust and hypocrisy argument.

picks.title: Xbox Has Looked Into Eliminating Paid Multiplayer – Report
picks.post:
According to a new report, Xbox looked into eliminating paid multiplayer as part of its Xbox Helix strategy.

The report says the idea was considered, not that it was decided.
picks.reason: Taking away a paid feature players already pay for is a classic fan-versus-company flashpoint.

picks.title: Call of Duty's Player Count Dropped by Over 40% Following GTA 6's Release, According to Analysts
picks.post:
A new analyst report says Call of Duty's player count fell by over 40% after GTA 6 launched.

The report ties the drop to GTA 6's release, which came out just days earlier.
picks.reason: Big franchise, big percentage, and a direct rivalry with GTA 6 that fans will argue over.

picks.title: Resident Evil creator Shinji Mikami says he wishes AI would disappear entirely, but that he experiments with it as a tool
picks.post:
Resident Evil creator Shinji Mikami says he wishes AI would disappear entirely, fearing mass job losses.

He still experiments with AI as a tool, and Stellar Blade's CEO shared a G-CON 2026 panel with opposing views.
picks.reason: A famous developer taking a bold stance on AI and jobs, with a public rival view.

picks.title: EXCLUSIVE: Some US banks tighten AI-agent controls on concern about models escaping safeguards
picks.post:
Some US banks are tightening controls on AI agents, software that acts on its own for users, Reuters reports.

The concern is that AI models could escape their safeguards.
picks.reason: Fear of AI escaping safeguards, tied to banks and customers' money, is an easy topic to take sides on.

picks.title: US to blacklist Asian AI firm Megaspeed after Nvidia scandal
picks.post:
The US plans to blacklist Asian AI firm Megaspeed over accusations it funneled AI chips to China.

The scandal began when a former Megaspeed executive's affair with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang became public.
picks.reason: Huang's affair scandal plus alleged chip smuggling to China gives a clear villain and a famous name.
picks.card_text: Accused of funneling AI chips to China

picks.title: Figma employee sues, alleging company forced her to confront harassers
picks.post:
Figma and its CEO are being sued by a current employee over alleged sexual harassment and discrimination.

She says the company forced her to confront the people harassing her.
picks.reason: Well-known app company and CEO accused of workplace harassment; people will pick sides on the company's response.

picks.title: More than 39 million people have played GTA 6 on PlayStation alone, Sony says, as the game breaks all-time player numbers on the platform
picks.post:
Sony says more than 39 million unique people have played GTA 6 on PlayStation alone.

That's more than the 32.5 million day-one sales Take-Two reported across all platforms.
picks.reason: A huge, specific number on GTA 6 that invites a fight over what player counts actually measure versus sales.

picks.title: Cyberleek releases executable for GTA 6 Xbox build leaked last week: 'The torch passes to the open source recomp and emulation projects'
picks.post:
Leaker CyberLeek has released the executable for a near-full GTA 6 Xbox build that leaked last week.

There is still no official PC version, and the torch has now passed to open source emulation projects.
picks.reason: Leak-versus-publisher tension on the most-hyped game, with fans split on piracy and an unannounced PC release.

picks.title: World stocks are mixed after Wall Street's rebound as Jensen Huang returns as Nvidia’s CEO
picks.post:
SpaceX and Tesla have appointed five directors to guide merger talks, the FT reports.

Both companies are run by Elon Musk, and no deal has been announced.
picks.reason: Musk running both sides of a possible merger invites strong opinions on fairness to shareholders.

picks.title: Big Tech could face billions of dollars in fines under Australian internet safety bill
picks.post:
Big Tech could face fines in the billions under an Australian internet safety bill.

The size of the penalties is the number that will split people over how far online platforms should be policed.
picks.reason: Billion-dollar fines on Big Tech for online safety draw strong views from users and critics.
picks.card_text: Fines could reach billions of dollars

picks.title: Dragon Age producer says BioWare struggled under EA because it had to keep choosing ‘the least terrible of the options’
picks.post:
A Dragon Age producer says BioWare struggled under EA because it kept choosing "the least terrible of the options."

Their explanation boils down to: you've got to hit your financials, so what are you going to do?
picks.reason: Pits BioWare's creative work against EA's profit demands, with a quote fans will share.

picks.title: Rockstar shuts down Discord server trying to make GTA 6 PC port
picks.post:
Rockstar Games has shut down a Discord server that was trying to build an unofficial PC port of GTA 6.

It follows CyberLeek's leak of GTA 6 Xbox build files, and there is still no official PC version.
picks.reason: Rockstar versus PC modders, with many fans desperate for GTA 6 on PC.

picks.title: Mass Effect Universe Would Have Answered Trilogy Ending Questions and Squadmate Fates, Writer Says
picks.post:
BioWare's canceled Mass Effect Universe would have answered questions about the Mass Effect 3 endings, a writer says.

It would also have addressed what happened to Shepard's squadmates.
picks.reason: A cancelled game tied to the most argued-over Mass Effect ending.
picks.card_text: Would have answered the ME3 endings

picks.title: Two billion credentials publicly exposed, including everything needed for identity theft
picks.post:
A security researcher has found a publicly exposed database holding about two billion login credentials.

It had no password protection or encryption, and it includes everything needed for identity theft.
picks.reason: Huge breach number with no password protection makes it a privacy story almost everyone feels.

screenshot_idea.text: 9to5Mac article on the exposed two billion credentials database

picks.title: Uber, Nuro, and Lucid kick off fully driverless robotaxi testing
picks.post:
Uber, Nuro and Lucid have started fully driverless robotaxi testing on public roads in the San Francisco Bay Area.

Employee-only rides launch shortly after, with no human driver behind the wheel.
picks.reason: Driverless cars on real roads hit safety fears and driver job worries at once.

screenshot_idea.text: Uber newsroom post on driverless testing with Nuro and Lucid

picks.title: Google Search’s AI Mode can now tap into Drive and Wallet for more personalized responses
picks.post:
Google says AI Mode in Search can now draw on your Google Drive and Wallet for more personalized answers.

It uses personal data Google already holds across its services, and the same feature is coming to the Gemini app.
picks.reason: Letting AI read personal files and wallet data raises an easy privacy fight.
picks.card_text: AI answers now draw on your Drive and Wallet

screenshot_idea.text: Google AI Mode settings page for personal intelligence

picks.title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit
picks.post:
UK disability minister Sir Stephen Timms has published his review of Pip, the personal independence payment, along with recommended changes.

Pip helps disabled people with extra living costs, so any change lands directly on claimants.
picks.reason: Everyday UK benefit with a direct impact on millions of claimants; any change will split opinion.
picks.card_text: Timms review recommends changes to Pip

screenshot_idea.text: GOV.UK page for the Timms review of PIP

images.credit: Steph Gray from London, United Kingdom

picks.title: Xbox Project Helix Was Reportedly Designed To Make Online Multiplayer Free
picks.post:
According to Windows Central, Microsoft's next Xbox, Project Helix, was designed to make online multiplayer free.

Online play on Xbox has been behind a paywall for years, through Xbox Live and Game Pass.
picks.reason: Free vs paid online play on Xbox is a fight players already have strong opinions about.
picks.card_text: Online multiplayer free on Project Helix

screenshot_idea.text: Windows Central report on Project Helix free multiplayer

picks.title: Performance analysis reveals GTA 6 has a more stable frame-rate on Xbox Series X compared to PlayStation 5
picks.post:
Performance analysis from Digital Foundry finds GTA 6 holds its 30fps target more steadily on Xbox Series X than on the base PS5.

If you don't own a PS5 Pro, the analysis says Xbox is the reported best way to play.
picks.reason: Console loyalists on both sides will argue over which version runs better.
picks.card_text: More stable 30fps on Xbox Series X

screenshot_idea.text: Digital Foundry GTA 6 performance analysis page

picks.title: Analyst estimates Call of Duty lost 44% of its players when GTA 6 came out, and unlike fans of its live-service competitors they've been slow to come back
picks.post:
An analyst estimates Call of Duty lost 44% of its players when GTA 6 came out.

Unlike fans of rival live-service games, Call of Duty players have been slow to come back.
picks.reason: A huge franchise losing nearly half its players to one game sparks instant debate.

screenshot_idea.text: Analyst estimate of Call of Duty player drop after GTA 6

picks.title: EA adds AI-generated John Motson to FC 27 video game
picks.post:
EA is adding an AI-generated John Motson to its football game EA Sports FC 27, from 26 November.

The move has the consent of Motson's son and wife, but it puts a famous commentator's voice into a game through AI.
picks.reason: Famous commentator, AI replacing a real voice, and a consent angle people will argue over.
picks.card_text: Consent from his son and wife

screenshot_idea.text: EA's official announcement of the AI Motson in FC 27

picks.title: Tidal to ban and remove millions of AI-generated tracks as AI slop inundates music streaming
picks.post:
Tidal will ban AI-generated music from 9 December and delete around 29 million AI-generated songs.

It expects to reject 80,000 to 85,000 tracks a day. Songs made with some AI help will still be accepted.
picks.reason: Huge deletion number and a streaming service drawing a line on AI music people pay for.

screenshot_idea.text: Tidal's AI music policy announcement

picks.title: Trump reportedly says pardoning Jensen Huang is ‘an option’
picks.post:
Trump has reportedly said pardoning Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is "an option."

Huang faces questions about his ties to Alice Huang, an executive with alleged links to Chinese intelligence.
picks.reason: Trump, Nvidia's CEO and a possible pardon make a politically charged story people will pick sides on.

screenshot_idea.text: TechCrunch report on Trump and a possible Huang pardon

picks.title: Energy bills to rise by 26% from January after gas prices surge
picks.post:
Energy bills are set to rise 26% from January after gas prices surged.

For a typical household, the annual bill would go from £1,723 to £2,166 if that level lasts a full year.

That is an extra £443 a year.
picks.reason: Everyone pays energy bills, and a 26% jump with a clear yearly cost will split people.

screenshot_idea.text: Ofgem announcement page on the energy price cap

images.credit: Impact of a commodity price shock on average household energy bills in advanced economies in 2030 by scenario by International Energy Agency (wikimedia)
Annual energy bill increase in the UK by IEA (wikimedia)

picks.title: Capcom dinosaur shooter Exoprimal's servers will go extinct next year, as shutdown meteor looms
picks.post:
Capcom is shutting down the online servers for its 2023 team shooter Exoprimal in late September 2027.

Once they go dark, the game won't be playable at all, even for people who already own it. It also gets pulled from stores in March.
picks.reason: A paid game being switched off within about two years leaves owners with nothing.

screenshot_idea.text: Official Exoprimal end-of-service notice

picks.title: Rust Will Officially Introduce Premium Paid Service With a Most-Requested Feature
picks.post:
Facepunch is adding a paid Rust Premium tier, and its perks include the game's most-requested feature: model customization.

The perks are in the staging test build for now. Players will decide whether the feature they asked for is worth paying for.
picks.reason: A paywall on a popular game's most-requested feature will split players straight away.

screenshot_idea.text: Rust Premium in the staging branch build notes

picks.title: Atari Homebrew Awards Canceled Over Torrent Of AI Games: ‘I Saw No Path Forward’
picks.post:
The Atari Homebrew Awards has been canceled after being flooded with AI-made game entries.

The cancellation statement says "I saw no path forward." It would have been the event's ninth year.
picks.reason: Indie game scene split over AI-generated games flooding a long-running event.

screenshot_idea.text: Atari Homebrew Awards cancellation statement

images.credit: Mahjong video game control panel 2023-04-13 by Asanagi (wikimedia)
New video game controller exposed by unknown (rawpixel)

picks.title: Microsoft declares a Code Red in response to worst ever outage
picks.post:
Microsoft says its recent Microsoft 365 outage was its worst ever, with more than 80% of servers unresponsive at the worst point.

It has now declared an internal "Code Red" to change how it prevents and responds to major failures.
picks.reason: Huge brand, record-breaking outage that hit millions of work and email users, and an unusually dramatic internal response.

screenshot_idea.text: Microsoft 365 service health page showing recent outage

images.credit: Argonite automatic fire suppression system server room by Froztbyte (wikimedia)
A view of the server room at The National Archives by The National Archives (UK) (wikimedia)

picks.title: Todoist confirms 6% of customers’ details were stolen in data breach
picks.post:
Todoist says a hacker stole customer data from 6% of its customers in a data breach.

The stolen data includes email addresses, password hashes and account creation dates.
picks.reason: Privacy breach at a popular app with password hashes exposed, which people care about directly.

screenshot_idea.text: Todoist's official breach notice or security update

images.credit: Healthcare Data Breaches Affecting 500 Individuals or More by Asyed49 (wikimedia)
San Francisquito Reservoir on topo v2 by Kbh3rd (wikimedia)

picks.title: In all-hands meeting, Jensen Huang thanks White House and says he’s in therapy
picks.post:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang says he's in therapy, in a staff all-hands on Tuesday.

He apologized to staff and thanked the White House, but reportedly told them it's "not true" Trump got him rehired.
picks.reason: Famous CEO saying something wild in the middle of a high-profile return saga that people already have strong opinions on.

screenshot_idea.text: TechCrunch story on Huang's all-hands remarks

picks.title: Airline Norse Atlantic says financial situation 'critical', shares plunge over 70%
picks.post:
Airline Norse Atlantic says its financial situation is 'critical', and its shares have plunged more than 70%.

Anyone with a booking on the airline now has a stake in what happens next.
picks.reason: Travellers with bookings are at risk, and a 70% share crash makes a possible airline collapse feel personal.

screenshot_idea.text: Norse Atlantic share price page showing the drop

images.credit: Global Hawk, NASA's New Remote-Controlled Plane by NASA Goddard Photo and Video (nasa)

picks.title: Ubisoft is reportedly requiring developers to justify not using generative AI
picks.post:
Ubisoft is reportedly requiring developers to justify not using generative AI.

The report says Ubisoft wants every project to use it, and staff who opt out must explain why.
picks.reason: Ubisoft plus forced generative AI is a flashpoint for both players and developers.

screenshot_idea.text: Report on Ubisoft requiring developers to justify not using generative AI

picks.title: Another Gaming Console Price Hike Could Be Coming, Thanks To New Tariffs
picks.post:
Proposed new US tariffs could mean another gaming console price rise.

China faces duties of up to 40% when they take effect next year, and Japan and the EU are also targeted.
picks.reason: Higher console prices hit every player's wallet and invite blame on companies and governments.

screenshot_idea.text: GameSpot article on new tariffs and possible console price hike

picks.title: Why GTA 6 Doesn’t Let You Replay Missions–It Felt “Alien And Disconnected”
picks.post:
Rockstar has left mission replay out of GTA 6, a feature that GTA 5 and Red Dead Redemption 2 both had.

Senior design director Scott Butchard says replays would have felt "alien and disconnected".
picks.reason: Fans of GTA 5 and Red Dead 2 will split over losing a beloved feature for story reasons.

screenshot_idea.text: GameSpot article on why GTA 6 has no mission replay

picks.title: Rockstar Games employees vote against union recognition
picks.post:
Around 75% of Rockstar Games' UK staff have voted against formal union recognition.

The vote came days after GTA 6's record launch, and the organisers say they will keep fighting.
picks.reason: Union defeat at the studio behind GTA 6 splits workers, fans and critics on labour rights.

screenshot_idea.text: IWGB statement on the Rockstar union vote result

picks.title: Microsoft-Owned Github Deletes Unhinged Post Celebrating PlayStation 5 Emulator’s Success Following Launch Of GTA 6
picks.post:
Microsoft-owned GitHub has deleted a post that celebrated a PS5 emulator passing 58K stars right after mentioning GTA 6.

The emulator is used to make unofficial PC ports of console games.
picks.reason: Big tech brand caught celebrating piracy-adjacent tool, then deleting it, fuels distrust.

screenshot_idea.text: Deleted GitHub post about the AnyPS5 emulator

picks.title: Simpsons Hit & Run and Prototype Studio Have Just Had Their Unannounced Game Canceled
picks.post:
Simpsons Hit & Run and Radical Entertainment have had an unannounced game canceled, according to one developer on social media.

Fans had been speculating about a Simpsons Hit & Run remake since Matt Groening suggested it was coming.
picks.reason: Beloved classic franchise and a cancelled project that fans were hoping for.

screenshot_idea.text: Developer social media post about the canceled game

picks.title: Is Alice Huang a spy or not?
picks.post:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is at the centre of a scandal over an affair with Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive.

The central claim that she is a Chinese spy is still unproven, and it is what the whole story turns on.
picks.reason: Famous CEO, affair plus espionage claim, and a clear unproven accusation people will pick sides on.

screenshot_idea.text: TechCrunch article on the Alice Huang Nvidia scandal

picks.title: X finally gets parental controls after 20 years
picks.post:
Elon Musk's social network X has finally added parental controls for teenagers.

It took X around 20 years to offer tools that let parents and guardians manage what their kids see on the platform.
picks.reason: Musk's X and kids' safety; many will argue it came too late or is not enough.

screenshot_idea.text: X help page on parental controls for teen accounts

picks.title: Android app developers will soon have to share their address publicly
picks.post:
Google will require many independent Android app developers to share a phone number and home address publicly from next year.

Developers say it is a privacy risk for small creators, while Google says the rule is needed to meet EU Digital Services Act rules.
picks.reason: Privacy hit for ordinary developers, with Google citing EU law; a clear fairness debate.
picks.card_text: Phone number and address, made public

screenshot_idea.text: Google Play developer policy page on contact details
